user_input: What happens if unforeseen exceptional circumstances make contract performance excessively burdensome for the debtor?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 147]
The contract makes the law of the parties. It can be
revoked or altered only by mutual consent of the parties
or for reasons provided for by law.
When, however, as a result of exceptional and
unpredictable events of a general character, the
performance of the contractual obligation, without
becoming impossible, becomes excessively onerous in
such way as to threaten the debtor with exorbitant loss,
the judge may according to the circumstances, and after
taking into consideration the interests of both parties,
reduce to reasonable limits, the obligation that has
become excessive. Any agreement to the contrary is
void.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 217]
The debtor may by agreement accept liability for
unforeseen events and for cases of force majeure. The
debtor may by agreement be discharged from all liability
for his failure to perform the contractual obligation, with
the exception of liability arising from his fraud or gross
negligence.
The debtor may, nevertheless, stipulate that he shall not
be liable for fraud or gross negligence committed by
persons whom he employs for the performance of his
obligation.
Any clause discharging a person from responsibility for
unlawful acts, is void.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 215]
When specific performance by the debtor is impossible,
he will be condemned to pay damages for
nonperformance of his obligation, unless he establishes
that the impossibility of performance arose from a cause
beyond his control. The same principle will apply, if the
debtor is late in the performance of his obligation.
response: If unforeseen exceptional circumstances make contract performance excessively burdensome for the debtor, the judge may, according to the circumstances and after taking into consideration the interests of both parties, reduce to reasonable limits the obligation that has become excessive. This is provided for in Article 147.
reference: The judge may, according to the circumstances and after weighing both parties' interests, reduce the excessive obligation to a reasonable limit. Any agreement to the contrary is void.

user_input: ماذا يحدث إذا جعلت ظروف استثنائية غير متوقعة تنفيذ العقد مرهقاً للمدين؟
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 147]
( ١ ( العقد شريعة المتعاقدين ، فلا يجوز نقضه ولا تعديله إلا باتفاق
الطرفين ، أو للأسباب التى يقررها القانون.
( ٢ ( ومع ذلك إذا طرأت حوادث استثنائية عامة لم يكن فى الوسع توقعها
وترتب على حدوثها أن تنفيذ الإلتزام التعاقدى ، وان لم يصبح مستحيلا ،
صار مرهقا للمدين بحيث يهدده بخسارة فادحة ، جاز للقاضى تبعا
للظروف وسد الموازنة بين مصلحة الطرفين أن يرد الإلتزام المرهق إلى
الحد المعقول. ويقع باطلا كل اتفاق على خلاف ذلك.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 217]
( ١ ( يجوز الاتفاق على أن يتحمل المدين تبعة الحادث المفاجئ والقوة
القاهرة.
( ٢ ( وكذلك يجوز الاتفاق على إعفاء المدين من أية مسئولية تترتب على
عدم تنفيذ إلتزامه التعاقدى الا ما ينشأ عن غشه أو عن خطئه الجسيم ، ومع
ذلك يجوز للمدين أن يشترط عدم مسئوليته عن الغش أو الخطأ الجسيم
الذى يقع من أشخاص يستخدمهم فى تنفيذ إلتزامه.
( ٣ ( ويقع باطلا كل شرط يقضى بالإعفاء من المسئولية المترتبة على
العمل غير المشروع.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 157]
( ١ ( فى العقود الملزمة للجانبين ، إذا لم يوف أحد المتعاقدين بإلتزامه جاز
للمتعاقد الآخر بعد اعذاره المدين أن يطالب بتنفيذ العقد أو بفسخه ، مع
التعويض فى الهالتين أن كان له مقتض.
( ٢ ( ويجوز للقاضى أن يمنح المدين اجلا إذا اقتضت الظروف ذلك ، كما
يجوز له أن يرفض الفسخ إذا كان ما لم يرف به المدين قليل الأهمية
بالنسبة إلى الإلتزام فى جملته.
response: إذا جعلت ظروف استثنائية غير متوقعة تنفيذ العقد مرهقاً للمدين، جاز للقاضى تبعا للظروف وسد الموازنة بين مصلحة الطرفين أن يرد الإلتزام المرهق إلى الحد المعقول. ويقع باطلا كل اتفاق على خلاف ذلك. (المادة 147)
reference: The judge may, according to the circumstances and after weighing both parties' interests, reduce the excessive obligation to a reasonable limit. Any agreement to the contrary is void.

user_input: In the absence of an applicable legal provision, what does the judge decide according to?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 1]
Provisions of laws govern all matters to which these
provisions apply in letter or spirit.
In the absence of a provision of a law that is applicable,
the Judge will decide according to custom and in the
absence of custom in accordance with the principles of
Moslem Law.
In the absence of such principles, the Judge will apply the
principles of natural justice and the rules of equity.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 200]
The judge shall decide, in the absence of any provision of
the law, whether a natural obligation exists.
There cannot ever be a natural obligation that is contrary
to public policy.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 346]
In the absence of an agreement or of a provision of the
law to the contrary, payment must be made as soon as
the obligation has been definitely created as a liability of
the debtor.
The judge may in exceptional cases and in the absence of
a provision of the law to the contrary, grant to the
debtor, when his position so requires, one or more
reasonable delays for the performance of his obligation,
provided that no serious prejudice is thereby caused to
the creditor.
response: In the absence of an applicable legal provision, the judge decides according to custom. If there is no custom, the judge decides in accordance with the principles of Moslem Law. If there are no such principles, the judge applies the principles of natural justice and the rules of equity. (Article 1)
reference: The judge decides according to custom, and in the absence of custom, according to the principles of Islamic (Moslem) law, and in the absence of such principles, according to natural justice and equity.

user_input: إذا لم يوجد نص تشريعي ينطبق على مسألة معينة، فبماذا يحكم القاضي؟

(١) تسرى النصوص التشريعية على جميع المسائل التي تتناولها هذه

فبمقتضى مبادئ القانون الطبيعي وقواعد العدالة.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 200]
يقدر القاضى ، عند عدم النص ، ما إذا كان هناك إلتزام طبيعى. وفى كل

يسرى في شأن المفقود والغائب الأحكام المقررة في قوانين خاصة ، فان لم

response: إذا لم يوجد نص تشريعي ينطبق على مسألة معينة، فيحكم القاضي بمقتضى العرف. وإذا لم يوجد العرف، فيحكم القاضي بمقتضى مبادئ الشريعة الإسلامية. وإذا لم يوجد مبادئ الشريعة الإسلامية، فيحكم القاضي بمقتضى مبادئ القانون الطبيعي وقواعد العدالة. هذا ما ورد في المادة ١ من القانون المدني المصري.
reference: The judge decides according to custom, and in the absence of custom, according to the principles of Islamic (Moslem) law, and in the absence of such principles, according to natural justice and equity.

user_input: How can a legal provision be repealed?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 2]
A provision of a law can only be repealed by a
subsequent law expressly providing for such repeal, or
containing a provision inconsistent with a provision of
the former law or regulating anew a matter previously
regulated by a former law.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 845]
Partition by agreement may be rescinded if one of the
co-partitioners succeeds in proving that he has been
injured to the extent of more than one fifth of his share,
on the basis of the value of the property at the time of
the partition.
The action for rescission must be commenced within the
year following the partition. The defendant can stop the
action and prevent the new partition, by giving the
plaintiff the amount by which his share is short in money
or in kind.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 149]
When a contract of adhesion contains leonine
conditions, the judge may modify these conditions or
relieve the adhering party of the obligation to perform
these conditions in accordance with the principles of
equity. Any agreement to the contrary is void.
response: A legal provision can only be repealed by a subsequent law that expressly provides for such repeal, or by a subsequent law containing a provision inconsistent with a provision of the former law or regulating anew a matter previously regulated by a former law. This is stipulated in Article 2 of the Egyptian Civil Code.
reference: A provision of law can only be repealed by a subsequent law that expressly provides for repeal, contains a provision inconsistent with the earlier law, or regulates anew a matter already regulated by the earlier law.

user_input: At what age does a person reach legal majority in Egypt?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 33]
Egyptian nationality is governed by a special law.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 44]
All persons attaining majority in possession of their
mental faculties and not under legal disability, have full
legal capacity to exercise their civil rights.
The majority of a person is fixed at twenty one years
completed in accordance with the Gregorian calendar.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 11]
The status and the legal capacity of persons are
governed by the law of the country to which they belong
by reason of their nationality. If, however, in a
transaction of a pecuniary nature, concluded and having
effect in Egypt, one of the parties is a foreigner without
legal capacity and such lack of capacity is due to a
reason that is not apparent and which cannot be easily
detected by the other party, this reason has no effect on
his legal capacity.
The legal status of foreign juristic persons such as
companies, associations, foundations, or others, is
subject to the law of the State in whose territory such
juristic persons have established their actual principal
seat of management. If, however, a juristic person
carries on its principal activities in Egypt, Egyptian law
will be applied.
response: In Egypt, a person reaches legal majority at the age of twenty one years completed, as stipulated in Article 44.
reference: A person attaining majority in possession of their mental faculties, and not under legal disability, has full legal capacity. Majority is fixed at twenty-one complete Gregorian years.

user_input: في أي سن يبلغ الشخص سن الرشد القانوني في مصر؟

يكون كامل الأهلية لمباشرة حقوقه المدنية.
(٢) وسن الرشد هى إحدى وعشرون سنة ميلادية كاملة.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 46]
كل من بلغ سن التمييز ولم يبلغ سن الرشد وكل من بلغ سن الرشد وكان
سفيهاً أو ذا غفلة ' يكون ناقص الأهلية وفقاً لما يقرره القانون.

(١) لا يكون أهلا لمباشرة حقوقه المدنية من كان فاقد التمييز لصغر في

reference: A person attaining majority in possession of their mental faculties, and not under legal disability, has full legal capacity. Majority is fixed at twenty-one complete Gregorian years.

user_input: What does Article 43 say?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 43]
A special domicile may be elected for the performance of
a specific legal act.
The election of domicile must be evidenced by writing.
A domicile elected for the performance of a legal act
shall be deemed to be the domicile in so far as all
matters relating to such act are concerned, including the
procedure for enforcement by legal means unless the
election of domicile is expressly limited to certain special
acts, excluding others.

[Egyptian Civil Code, Articles 54-80] (REPEALED -- no longer in force)
* Articles 54-80 have been repealed by Presidential
Decree.
SECTION III
The Classification of Things and Property

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 599]
If, after the lease has expired, the lessee continues to
enjoy the leased property to the knowledge of and
without objection on the part of the lessor, the lessee is
deemed to be renewed upon the same conditions but
for an indefinite duration. The lease so renewed is
governed by the provisions of Article 563.
The tacit renewal is deemed to be a new lease and not a
mere prolongation of the original lease. Nevertheless,
subject to the rules of publication applicable to real
property, the real securities supplied by the lessee in
guarantee of the old lease are transferred to the new
lease. The suretyship, whether personal or real, is not
transferred to the new lease unless the surety consents
thereto.
response: Article 43 states that a special domicile may be elected for the performance of a specific legal act. The election of domicile must be evidenced by writing. A domicile elected for the performance of a legal act shall be deemed to be the domicile in so far as all matters relating to such act are concerned, including the procedure for enforcement by legal means unless the election of domicile is expressly limited to certain special acts, excluding others.
reference: It concerns the domicile of a missing or absent person, and the special domicile of a minor who has attained eighteen years for acts they are legally capable of performing.

user_input: What does Article 274 say?
retrieved_contexts:
[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 274]
An obligation with a suspensive term only becomes due
on the date of the expiration of the term. The creditor
may, however, even before the end of the term, take
measures to protect his rights and may, in particular, ask
for security if he fears that the debtor may become
bankrupt or insolvent, and has reasonable grounds for
his fears.
At the end of a resolutory term, the obligation is
extinguished without such extinction having any
retroactive effect.
Section II
Plurality of Objects of an Obligation
1. Alternative Obligations

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 1108]
The provisions of Article 1050, relating to the
responsibility of a mortgagor who is not a debtor, and
the provisions of Article 1052, relating to appropriation
in case of non-payment and to sale without recourse to
legal formalities, apply to pledge.
2- As Regards Third Parties

[Egyptian Civil Code, Article 980]
The owner to whom the property is restituted must pay
to the possessor all the expenditure of a necessary kind
that he has incurred.
The provisions of Articles 924 and 925 shall apply as
regard expenditure of an advantageous kind.
If the expenditure is of a luxurious nature, the possessor
cannot claim repayment of any of such expenditure. He
may, however, remove works he has made, provided he
restores the property to its original condition, unless the
owner prefers to keep the works upon payment of their
break up value.
response: Article 274 states that an obligation with a suspensive term only becomes due on the date of the expiration of the term. The creditor may, however, even before the end of the term, take measures to protect his rights and may, in particular, ask for security if he fears that the debtor may become bankrupt or insolvent, and has reasonable grounds for his fears. At the end of a resolutory term, the obligation is extinguished without such extinction having any retroactive effect.
reference: An obligation with a suspensive term becomes due on the date the term expires; before that, the creditor may take measures to protect his rights if he fears the debtor may become insolvent.
